facts.fact: Pollicy says Morocco's Law No. 31-13 on the right to access information came into full effect in 2020.

Commission president Omar Seghrouchni said at a Kenitra meeting that effective application of Law 31.13 depends on better knowledge of its provisions, and commission member Abderrahim Fakkahi criticised the wording of its Article 10.
The Commission du droit d'accès à l'information (CDAI), with a president and members, held a regional meeting at Kenitra on 7 November 2026 as the body overseeing the right of access.

facts.fact: Minister Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni told parliament that the current Law No. 31-13 on the right of access to information lets citizens submit direct requests to public bodies.
The minister said the Commission du droit d'acces a l'information is charged with ensuring the right is exercised, handling complaints, advising and writing an annual report on implementation.

facts.fact: Carnegie's Soukina Nait El-Rayes writes that Morocco's Right to Information Law 31.13 was enacted nearly seven years earlier and sets 20-working-day deadlines for answering requests.
Carnegie's Soukina Nait El-Rayes writes that the prime minister appointed the members of the right to access information commission on 13 March 2019, and that it has issued no report since.
ARTICLE 19 says Morocco's Law 31-13 on the Right to Access Information, adopted in 2018, came into effect in March 2020.
